title: Reservoir-backed block allocator and pin-coalescer to reduce KV cache churn
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Introduces a reservoir-backed block allocator and a pin-coalescer that reduces KV cache churn and lowers tail latency. Backwards-compatible; enabled behind runtime flag by default for new clusters.
description:
Motivation: Frequent small pin/unpin operations in our paged KV cache cause allocator metadata churn and increased eviction IO during high-concurrency workloads (continuation-heavy decoding). This PR introduces a lightweight reservoir-backed block allocator plus a pin-coalescer layer to reduce metadata updates and contention, and adds a kernel scheduling hint to prioritize hot pinned lanes. The design goals were: 1) reduce allocator metadata operations under bursty access patterns; 2) keep average allocation latency unchanged; 3) reduce eviction IO and tail latency for real serving workloads; 4) remain opt-in behind a runtime feature flag until bake.

Summary of changes:
- Implement ReservoirBlockAllocator: per-lane mini-pools that refill/return to a global reservoir to reduce global lock pressure. Allocation fast-path is lock-free for hot-path requests that can be satisfied from the lane reservoir; slow-path obtains from global reservoir with backoff and batching.
- Add PinCoalescer: when multiple adjacent small pins occur within a short epoch, coalesce them into a single metadata update to the block manager (reduces journal writes). Coalescer uses a bounded ring and epoch commit semantics to avoid long-lived pins.
- Kernel scheduling hint: the allocator exposes a hotness score for lanes (based on pin frequency); scheduler's priority queue (priority hints only) uses this to prefer pinned-hot lanes to avoid repeated cold fills.
- Tests & bench: microbench harness for continuous-batching-decoder scenarios, integration test to validate correctness under races, and a stress test to assert eviction stability under heavy pin churn.
- Operational: docs/allocator.md documents tunables and suggested defaults; a runtime flag enable_reservoir_allocator toggles behavior per-cluster.

Commits (high-level):
- feat(kv): add ReservoirBlockAllocator with per-lane reservoirs
- feat(kv): add PinCoalescer and epoch commit logic
- perf(kv): expose lane_hotness metric and scheduler hint integration
- test(kv): add reservoir and coalescer unit/integration tests
- bench: add continuous-batching decoder microbench and results harness
- fix(lint): address clippy warnings and unify error handling
- ci: update pipeline to add deterministic bench job for perf regressions

Files changed (high level):
- src/kv/block_allocator.rs (new core allocator implementation & comments)
- src/kv/pin_coalescer.rs (new coalescer with bounded ring buffer)
- runtime/scheduler/priority_queue.rs (hook to read lane_hotness hints)
- runtime/config/flags.rs (runtime flag enable_reservoir_allocator)
- tests/bench/reservoir_bench.rs (microbench harness)
- tests/integration/kv_eviction_stress.rs (race and eviction stability tests)
- docs/allocator.md (operational notes and defaults)

Microbenchmark results (CI deterministic bench run):
- Continuous-batching decoder (50 concurrent lanes, seq_len 256, batch target 8): p50 tokens/ms improved by ~12%, p95 reduced by ~18%, p99 reduced by ~22%
- Eviction IO: measured 18% fewer metadata writes in benchmark scenario; net IO decrease on SSD-backed cache nodes.
- CPU overhead: reservoir allocator adds ~1.2% steady-state CPU due to maintenance/refill; net throughput gains offset this in busy workloads.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Reservoir size per-lane is configurable; default chosen conservatively to avoid memory bloat on low-load nodes.
- Coalescer epoch is time-bounded (default 50ms) to avoid delaying pin visibility for readers. This introduces a tunable latency knob; defaults were validated on CI-benches and a small canary.
- Consistency model: pin coalescing does not change observable semantics (pins are still honored) — coalescing only batches metadata writes but commits them with epoch guarantees.
- Fallbacks: under memory pressure or if the reservoir empties, allocator falls back to global slow-path which preserves correctness.

Rollout plan: default enabled for new clusters; existing clusters can opt-in via console flag. We will roll canary to 5% traffic for 72h, monitor lane_hotness, eviction_write_rate, and p99 token latency before broad rollout.

Review conversation (selected threads): "Arjun Patel: Nice design. Two quick things: 1) can you add a safety check to ensure epochs don't starve readers? 2) what are memory bloat protections for misbehaving lanes?" "Author (Maya): Added epoch max-duration (50ms) and a max-reservoir-per-lane cap with eviction into global reservoir. Updated docs/allocator.md with recommended limits and rationale." "Sofia Liu: CI bench shows good wins but the priority hint coupling looked invasive. Please ensure scheduler fallback if hint source fails." "Author (Maya): Priority hint is advisory-only; scheduler still uses load-based fallback. Added comment and test to validate fallback behavior (priority_queue tests)." "Rajesh Nair: Found a race in coalescer commit path during stress run (two-epoch handoff)." "Author (Maya): Fixed with an atomic epoch swap + commit barrier; added reproducer test and stress-run in CI." "CI bot: Initial pipeline failed linter and flaky bench job timed out. Author pushed fix and retriggered. Final CI: all green including deterministic bench job." "SRE: Please add a dashboard for lane_hotness and eviction_write_rate before wide rollout." "Author: Dashboard tiles added to observability-pack; documented alert thresholds in docs/allocator.md."

CI summary: initial run had 1 lint failure and one flaky bench timeout; fixes were pushed and final run passed. Merge strategy: squash-and-merge after approvals and green CI. Impact statement: Expected to reduce tail latency and metadata IO in production serving workloads with heavy prefix reuse or continuous batching. No API changes to callers; feature is behind a runtime flag for safe rollouts.
